NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences, immediate intent, and recurring interests. [MSMT-LSI (2024)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44196-024-00460-5) combines separate long- and short-term attention networks with multiple temporal embeddings. [Denoising Long- and Short-term Interests (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) models session-level interest evolution and uses contrastive augmentation to reduce incidental-interaction noise. [MIMAR-SRec (2026)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489) learns intent representations across contextual windows, aligning sequences with intent prototypes while adding robustness to interaction and temporal noise.

The closest match is [HyperHawkes (WWW 2025)](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/): contrastive clustering extracts latent intents; Hawkes processes model recurring intent and long-term preferences; a multi-level attention mixture captures immediate interests. Its key implication: elapsed time need not imply monotonically declining relevance—some interests recur. An architecture hypothesis for this benchmark is a lightweight SASRec extension combining recent-context features, pooled historical preferences, and a small latent-intent bank through a learned gate conditioned on observed time gaps. Compare learned decay against a decay-plus-recurrence variant. Treat purchase saturation as an unverified hypothesis, not an observed satisfaction signal; histories alone do not establish why interest changed. Under unseen-item recommendation, intent recurrence can transfer to related unseen products even when exact-item repetition cannot contribute. These adaptations are proposals, not established gains on the pinned benchmark.

---

Evidence supports testing the loss before increasing capacity. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) attributes SASRec weaknesses to overconfidence induced by negative sampling; recommends generalized BCE with 128–256 negatives and correction parameter t=0.75. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) identifies sampled softmax combined with SASRec’s autoregressive objective and improved Transformer layers as a strong configuration. These findings motivate a controlled loss-only comparison; they do not establish that Electronics specifically suffers from easy negatives.

Hardness needs safeguards. [R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) samples randomly from a top-ranked candidate set instead of always selecting the highest-scoring item, with progressively harder selection to mitigate false negatives. Practical ablation proposal: uniform multi-negative sampled softmax first, then a mixture of uniform and moderately hard negatives after warm-up; exclude padding, target collisions, and known training positives from negative pools. These exclusions cannot identify every unobserved relevant item. For popularity or in-batch sampling, [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that proposal correction must account for the positive being included deterministically; sampling-bias correction is distinct from false-negative correction.

Compare baseline BCE, multi-negative BCE, gBCE, and sampled softmax with architecture held fixed, reporting GPU cost and per-category HR@10 alongside the four-category macro average. Select using the unchanged pinned validation protocol: 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, seed 42. Training margins alone cannot establish improvement. [Sampled-metric research](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/0651.pdf) shows sampled evaluation can reverse full-catalog model rankings, so gains here support this benchmark objective without establishing better full-catalog recommendations.

---

Most relevant lightweight lead: [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) constructs a directed, weighted item graph from interaction histories and purchase order, supporting neighborhood-based recommendation without pretrained representations. Useful inspiration for a sparse transition branch alongside SASRec; its complementarity interpretation remains a behavioral proxy, not proof of functional compatibility. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) models complementary relationships through both relevance and dissimilarity, using low-pass and mid-pass graph filters with attention. Key lesson: similarity-only aggregation can erase distinctions useful for complementary recommendations.

Recent metadata approaches often violate the available-data constraints. [KGSCL (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S089360802500070X) uses explicit Amazon substitution/complement relations for sequence augmentation; those relations are unavailable here. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines SASRec-style modeling with BERT-encoded titles, descriptions and reviews, requiring modification to remove pretrained weights and reviews. [MMSC (2025; revised 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22268) emphasizes that behavioral associations provide noisy supervision, but uses a multimodal foundation model and LLM-assisted supervision.

Constraint-compatible research direction, inferred from these papers: retain separate directed transition and symmetric text-similarity channels; encode titles/descriptions with randomly initialized token embeddings and pooling, then learn gated fusion with item IDs through next-item prediction.
